How do I ping this check?

Have your job call the URL above when it runs — a plain GET or POST reports success. Add a suffix for other signals:

SignalURLEffect
successhttp://localhost:18080/ping/40938239-02bd-44e1-8f21-09b9dd53309cmarks the check up
failhttp://localhost:18080/ping/40938239-02bd-44e1-8f21-09b9dd53309c/failmarks the check down
starthttp://localhost:18080/ping/40938239-02bd-44e1-8f21-09b9dd53309c/startopens a run so an overrun can be caught
loghttp://localhost:18080/ping/40938239-02bd-44e1-8f21-09b9dd53309c/logrecords a note, status unchanged
exit codehttp://localhost:18080/ping/40938239-02bd-44e1-8f21-09b9dd53309c/<code>0 = up, anything else = down
shell examples# report success when the job finishes curl -fsS http://localhost:18080/ping/40938239-02bd-44e1-8f21-09b9dd53309c # wrap a job: start it, run, then report the exit code curl -fsS http://localhost:18080/ping/40938239-02bd-44e1-8f21-09b9dd53309c/start mybackup.sh curl -fsS http://localhost:18080/ping/40938239-02bd-44e1-8f21-09b9dd53309c/$? # report failure and attach the output (shown in Recent pings) mybackup.sh 2>&1 | curl -fsS --data-binary @- http://localhost:18080/ping/40938239-02bd-44e1-8f21-09b9dd53309c/fail
oldersolid = timed run, taller = longer · hollow = duration not measurable · amber ≥80% budget · red = failednow
